Subject: RFI — commercial clarifications (seat bands / credits)

Vanessa,

Thanks for taking our RFI. Procurement at NovaMed had a couple of follow-ups specifically on the commercial/pricing section that we'd like clarified before we move to the next evaluation stage. The items that need short write-ups from Redwood are below — we'd appreciate a consolidated response and any sample pricing workbook you can share.

1) Seat / user banding: describe a banded seat model (bands, pricing tiers, how overages are calculated within a month). Can seats scale intra-month or do you only true-up monthly/quarterly?

2) Annualized credits: do you offer credits that are applied against overages when customers commit to an annualized consumption profile? Example: customer commits 12M baseline; how do credits apply if usage is uneven across months?

3) Rolling true-up vs fixed true-up: we prefer rolling monthly true-ups but some vendors require annual true-ups. What does Redwood support, and what are the invoice implications?

4) Discount stack: explain how discounts (commit volume, multi-year, and term) stack. Are there any exclusions (e.g., burst overage rates)?

5) Billing example: provide a worked example for a 1,000-seat cohort with 30% usage variance month-to-month and a 1.2B token annual commit.

We attached our simplified RFI questions as a PDF for context.

Appreciate a response by EOD Thursday if possible — the evaluation committee meets Friday.

Best,
John

NovaMed Health Systems

John — thanks for the clear list. Tagging Marissa (pricing) and Ben (solutions) to pull together the workbook and a short narrative addressing each of your bullets.

High-level now: Redwood supports intra-month seat adjustments, offers an annualized credit program that smooths overage exposure for front-loaded or back-loaded consumption, and supports monthly rolling true-ups as a supported billing cadence (we can also do quarterly or annual if required). Discounts are applied in a deterministic order: committed volume first, then multi-year/term incentives, then any transaction-level concessions. Exclusions typically apply to burst overage rates — we'll call those out explicitly.

We'll get a formal workbook and a worked billing example to you within 48 hours. Quick question for the billing example: do you want invoiced amounts shown net of credits and discounts, or a gross -> net waterfall?

Folks — attaching the pricing workbook that addresses John’s 5 points. Key notes included in the first tab (Executive Summary). I’ll paste the short answers here as well so they’re in-line with the RFI: 

- Seat banding: Standard bands are 1-250 / 251-1,000 / 1,001-5,000 with per-seat equivalents for API-only access. Overages are charged at the band rate prorated daily; intra-month seat adds are billed pro-rata for the remainder of the month and counted toward monthly consumption for usage-based true-up.

- Annualized credits: We provide an Annualized Credit (AC) applied to monthly overages when a customer commits to a 12-month consumption baseline. Credits are earned proportionally to unused committed tokens and applied to overage charges in months where usage exceeds the monthly baseline. Credits roll across months within the 12M period but expire at contract end unless otherwise negotiated.

- Rolling true-up: Redwood supports monthly rolling true-ups by default. With rolling true-ups, invoices reflect month-end usage and any overage/credit adjustments are on the next invoice cycle. If customers prefer an annual true-up, we can defer invoicing until contract-level reconciliation, but that requires booking a larger committed bucket and different accounting recognition.

- Discount stacking: Discounts apply in this order: committed volume discount -> multi-year/term incentive -> channel/partner credit -> one-time concessions. Burst overages are excluded from committed volume discounts and are billed at a higher overage rate; however, those overage rates can be capped via a Burst Cap addendum.

- Billing example: see tab "Worked Example". Net waterfall included (gross usage -> discounts -> credits -> final invoice). I've included both Net-of-Credits and Gross->Net views.

Thanks Marissa — the workbook is helpful. A couple of clarifying follow-ups before we circulate to finance: 

1) Band overflow: if a cohort grows from 240 to 260 mid-month, do you retroactively re-seat the entire cohort at the next month's band price or only apply band pricing to the increment? We prefer the latter but need to understand how revenue is recognized.

2) Credit expiry: you mentioned credits expire at contract end. Can credits be negotiated to a 6-month expiry or to transfer to a renewal?

3) Invoice presentation: our finance team requires a Gross->Net invoice line-by-line (gross usage, committed discount, multi-year discount, credits applied, net due). Can you provide a sample PDF invoice demonstrating your standard layout?

4) One more — for the rolling true-up, what is the SLA for dispute resolution? If we dispute an overage, how is it handled on the subsequent invoice?

If you can get answers + a sample invoice by EOD Thursday that would be great.

John / Lisa — thanks for the quick follow-ups. Answers below + attached a sample invoice and a short Mutual Action Appendix (MAA) that captures proposed rolling true-up cadence and dispute SLA.

1) Band overflow: we charge incremental units at the new band rate (i.e., only the delta is billed at the higher band for the remainder of the month). At the following month’s billing, the cohort’s baseline will be evaluated and, if sustained growth persists, the baseline seat band will move forward. Revenue recognition: we invoice pro-rata for the month; recognized revenue treatment follows standard ASC guidance (we can provide language for your accounting team if needed).

2) Credit expiry: standard practice is expiry at contract end. We can offer a negotiated 6-month carry-forward on a renewal at the point of contract renewal (common for enterprise renewals). Transfer of credits to a renewal can be included as a negotiated term in the MSA — Marissa included optional language in the MAA attachment.

3) Invoice presentation: attached sample invoice includes Gross->Net line items and a separate CSV extract format that maps to GL fields. We can include additional custom fields on invoices for GL mapping (e.g., cost center tag, purchase order, department).

4) Dispute SLA: standard SLA is 30 calendar days from invoice date to raise a dispute. Disputes are handled on the following invoice cycle: disputed amount is noted, and if unresolved by the next cycle we place a provisional credit while we investigate. For high-value disputes we can agree to a 15-day SLT in the MAA.

Attachments: MAA_NovaMed_v1.docx (contract appendix), Sample_Invoice_NovaMed_GrossToNet.pdf (sample invoice)
